text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This paper presents a national-scale GIS-based land use model (LAND USE SCANNER) applied to the entire Netherlands, explicitly simulating future land use under multiple scenarios (Divided Europe, European Co-ordination, Global Competition) with quantitative spatial outputs including mapped LULC projections. The primary focus is on LULC prediction/simulation, particularly residential construction as a major driver of land use change, with integration of environmental impact assessment. The methodology includes spatially explicit modeling at 500m grid resolution, scenario-based quantitative comparison, and the use of suitability maps and balancing factors. Although quantitative accuracy metrics (e.g., statistical validation or accuracy assessments) are not explicitly detailed, the model calibration and regression analyses are presented, and the modeling framework is applied to produce future land use maps and environmental indicators. The study is not a review, is at national scale, and involves multiple scenarios with spatially explicit LULC projections, meeting core inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria.)
